codec.$comment: Frozen codec vocabulary. Fixed-width integers carry their endianness in the name; u8 is the one endian-free width. bytes(n) and fixed_string(n) match a pattern, and vec<T>/matrix<T> match a pattern whose element T is itself a vocabulary member. opaque(id) is the honest escape when an item's own text does not determine a codec: it is valid but blocks codegen. PREFIXED LENGTHS: prefixed_bytes and prefixed_string INCLUDE their length prefix -- the prefix varint is part of the codec itself -- so a separate prefix_varint field immediately before one of them double-counts the length and would make a code generator emit the prefix twice. The three compositional members (nested, counted, optional) each carry their own $comment below; together with the card-level `presence` block they are the whole of conditional, nested, counted records.

oneOf.$comment: NESTED RECORD: nested(<card uid>) is the body of another codec card, decoded and encoded by that card's own layout. It is how a record appears inside another record, so the inner layout is named once and never copied into the container. The named card must exist, must be a codec card with fields, and must not be unknown; a dangling name is a validation FAIL, not a silent opaque run.

COUNTED CONTAINER WITH ITS OWN ELEMENT LAYOUT: counted(<element>) is a prefix-varint element count followed by that many values, where <element> is a vocabulary member or a nested(<uid>) record. It is the generalisation of vec<T> to an element that has a layout of its own; a field-level `max` bounds the count.

OPTIONAL: optional(<codec>) is a STRICT zero-or-one flag byte followed by the value only when the flag is 1. A flag byte above 1 is refused, never read as true, because the client's own reader refuses it; this is the shape of a presence-flagged scalar and is not a count.

mask_level.$comment: ONE PRESENCE MASK BYTE: `name` is the generated field name for the mask (`group_mask`, `entry_mask`); `bits` is how many low-first bits carry members; `continuation`, when present, is the single bit above them that means a further mask byte follows. Exactly one mask byte per level is modelled, so a continuation bit is refused rather than followed.

presence.$comment: TWO-LEVEL PRESENCE MASK (conditional membership): a card with `presence` has no flat field order. Its body is [one group mask byte][for each present group: one member mask byte][the bodies of the present members, ascending by member index], and a field is on the wire only when both its group bit and its member bit are set -- declared per field as presence:{group,member}. This is the shape the client's own reader walks: one mask byte per chunk of eight groups, then within a present group a 7-bit member mask whose top bit means a further byte. A set bit that names a group or member the card does not declare is REFUSED, never skipped, so a wider mask cannot be silently misread.

field.$comment: CODEGEN-READY RULE: a card is codegen-ready iff it has at least one field and every field is where:'wire' with a type that is not opaque(...), and the card's own status is not unknown. partial does NOT block codegen; unknown and opaque do. A card with no fields[] is neither ready nor not-ready, so it must never count toward the codegen-ready number. BODY-ONLY RULE: fields[] describes the message BODY only. The record envelope is `[vlq32 length][00 01][prefix-varint type]`, generic framing owned by `services/world/src/azoth_world/javelin/frame.py` (and `bundle.py`); it must never appear as a field. Keep that knowledge in the card-level `envelope` string instead. MEMORY RULE: a where:'memory' field carries a decoded-struct offset, can never drive codegen, and must still declare a type (a vocabulary member, or opaque(id) when unknown).

meaning.$comment: How much we know about what this field CARRIES. `known`: we know what the field carries (its meaning), not just its bytes. `layout-only`: we know the bytes, type and offset but not the meaning -- an honest statement, not a failure. Exactly these two values, no third. A placeholder name (field_*, unresolved_*, unknown_*, raw*, blob*, head, *_at_0x*, or a name that is only a type or an offset) MUST be `layout-only` and may never claim `known`; a field claiming `known` must carry a `note` that says what it is. This marking is VISIBILITY, never a codegen gate: a `layout-only` field does not stop its card being code-generated.

presence.$comment: The conditional-membership coordinates of one field in a card that declares the two-level `presence` mask: the field is on the wire only when both mask bits are set. A card without `presence` may not put these coordinates on any field, and a card with `presence` may not leave a wire field without them.

fields.description: The message BODY only. The [vlq32 length][00 01][prefix-varint type] record envelope is framing owned by javelin/frame.py and is never a field; record it in the card-level `envelope` string.

envelope.description: Card-level record envelope text: the [vlq32 length][00 01][prefix-varint type] framing owned by javelin/frame.py, kept out of fields[] because fields[] is the body only.

legacy.description: Grandfathered card: at least one field item is still opaque or unknown, so its field items are exempt from the closed field schema.
